correctness.rationale: All original row/column/sum adjacency possibilities and stabilizer orbits are exhausted. The fixed-point triangulation is the orbit-clique complex because each orbit is a clique and the original complex is flag. The q diagonal vertices form one simplex, offdiagonal orbits split into q-1 sum-class simplices of q/2 vertices, and each offdiagonal orbit has precisely two diagonal neighbors. In each sum class a contractible side complex meets the preceding union in q/2 disjoint edges; both inclusions are nullhomotopic and cofibrations. Homotopy pushout gives q/2-1 new circles per class. Standalone exact tests check all orbit pairs for q=4,8,16,32; exhaustive small cliques and mod-two boundaries confirm ranks 3 and 21 for q=4,8, without substituting for the proof. In addition, explicit sequences of 10 and 176 elementary simplicial collapses produce connected graphs with the predicted cycle ranks at group orders 4 and 8, respectively.
